Changes Ahead at Renshaw Stationers
Local Business Section — By Ian Furlong
Millbrook, May 2
Frances Duvall, who opened Renshaw Stationers and has directed it ever since, will step back from daily management at the end of this month. Two members of her staff, Grace Abbott and Emil Kovacs, will take on the business jointly from June 1.
The store began in 1981 as a counter at the back of a printing works and has traded from its present address on the town's main business street for more than forty years. It supplies notebooks, filing materials, and desk equipment to local offices and to schools across the district.
Ms. Abbott began as a delivery driver and now keeps the accounts, while Mr. Kovacs has taken orders at the front counter for eighteen years. Staffing will remain as it is. "The name above the door will not change, and neither will the way we trade," Mr. Kovacs said.
The store will close on May 18 while new shelving is installed inside, and it will reopen at the same address on May 26. Orders may be placed by e-mail throughout the closure, with no charge added for delivery. Deliveries themselves begin again on the reopening day, and a customer who needs an order before then may collect it from the company's storage unit on Kestrel Lane.
Ms. Duvall will keep an office upstairs two mornings a week until December. "I would rather leave the store to people who helped build it than to a stranger," she said. "Our nine employees are all staying, and the work goes on as before."
